email.subject: MV DUNLIN GATE - Red Sea passage declined (war risks)
email.body:
Dear Operations,

MV DUNLIN GATE, Mundra to Gijon

Following the security advisory issued overnight on attacks on merchant ships in the southern Red Sea, owners have decided, in the reasonable judgement of the Master and owners, not to proceed through Bab el-Mandeb or the Red Sea. We rely on the war risks clause of the charter party.

Please give alternative orders. We propose the passage via the Cape of Good Hope. The Master has been told to keep well clear of the area while awaiting your orders.

Best regards,
Marine department
Owner's vessel technical management (Dunlin Gate Shipping, fictional)

The owner relies on the charter party's war risks clause: since the owners decided, in the reasonable judgement of the Master and/or the owners, that MV DUNLIN GATE must not pass Bab el-Mandeb or the Red Sea, she is not obliged to do so and the charterers must give other orders; the extra time and bunkers on the alternative route are for the charterers' account, i.e. your company. From the AIS position (19.958°N, 58.948°E, 22 Jan 06:00 UTC) the Cape of Good Hope route to Gijon is 9824 nm versus the planned 5023.2 nm — +4800.8 nm, +16 days at 12.5 kn — with a new ETA of 24 Feb 2025 00:00 UTC, +374 h on the planned ETA; these are the route checker's simulated figures for this demo. VLSFO on board (about 1433.7 t) covers the new route with about 556.1 t expected on arrival, above the 3-day reserve of 80.4 t, so there is no shortfall and no bunkers need to be arranged on the way. Nothing should be sent until you answer.

Extra time and bunkers on the alternative route are for the charterers' account under the war risks clause.

Please let us know if you require any further details.

Kind regards,
